newsitem.title: USA: Viacom stock jumps on share buyback plan.
newsitem.headline: Viacom stock jumps on share buyback plan.

text.p: The stock of Viacom Inc., owner of Blockbuster Video and cable channel MTV, jumped Thursday on news of a plan by the company and its top shareholder to buy back as much as 6 percent of the giant entertainment company's depressed stock.
The $500 million buyback comes just before a key meeting between analysts and company executives and marks the end of Viacom's long restriction on repurchases.

Viacom said the company, Chairman Sumner Redstone and his National Amusements Inc. intended to buy up to $500 million in Viacom shares and warrants -- $250 million by Viacom and up to $250 million by National or Redstone.

"It is a statement by the company that they consider the shares very undervalued," said Edward Hatch, an analyst at UBS Securities. "The buyback is split between a personal purchase by Redstone through National Amusements and Viacom itself."
Viacom's Class A shares were up almost 7 percent, or $2, to $32.375 on the American Stock Exchange -- down from a high of about $54 last September.
The timing of the buyback "comes after the first clearance they have had after the spinoff of the cable systems," Hatch said. "Share repurchases were restricted for some time because of that."

Viacom, which owns the video movie chain store Blockbuster Video and rock video television channel MTV Networks, spun off its cable operations, valued at $2.3 billion, to cable television giant Tele-Communications Inc. in a complex deal which closed on July 31.
"The company was not permitted to purchase shares while the deal was pending for over a year, and also was not able to do so immediately after" the deal closed, a source close to Viacom said.
The buyback announcement was made after a "comfort level" was reached regarding the end of restriction, as opposed to a specific "green light" date, the source said.
Hatch said that "based on the public float, it is a meaningful buyback of about 6 percent of outstanding shares across both classes, excluding what is owned by Redstone already."
National Amusements and Viacom will finance the repurchases from their working capital, they said.

National Amusements acquired control of Viacom in June 1987 and owns about 65 percent of Viacom's Class A shares and about 26 percent of the Class A and Class B common on a combined basis, according to Viacom.
Viacom said as of June 30 there were 69.9 million Class A shares and 286.7 million Class B shares outstanding.
